source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 10 (The Human Eye and the Colourful World).

sections.heading: 1. The Human Eye
points: The **human eye** is a natural optical instrument; the **cornea** and **lens** (a convex lens) focus light on the **retina**.
The **iris** controls the size of the **pupil** (amount of light entering); the **retina** has light-sensitive cells that send signals via the **optic nerve** to the brain.
**Power of accommodation** — the eye lens changes its focal length (via ciliary muscles) to focus objects at different distances.
**Near point** = 25 cm (least distance of distinct vision); **far point** = infinity (normal eye).

sections.heading: 2. Defects of Vision and Correction
points: **Myopia (short-sightedness)** — can see near but not distant objects; image forms **in front of** retina; corrected by a **concave lens**.
**Hypermetropia (long-sightedness)** — can see distant but not near objects; image forms **behind** retina; corrected by a **convex lens**.
**Presbyopia** — old-age weakening of accommodation (both near and far); corrected by **bifocal lenses**.
**Cataract** — clouding of the lens (blurred vision); corrected by surgery.

sections.heading: 3. Refraction Through a Prism & Dispersion
points: A **prism** bends light through an **angle of deviation** and **splits white light** into its colours = **dispersion** (VIBGYOR).
**Newton** showed white light is made of seven colours; a second inverted prism recombines them.
Cause of dispersion: different colours bend by different amounts (**red least, violet most**).
A **rainbow** is formed by dispersion + internal reflection + refraction of sunlight in water droplets after rain.

sections.heading: 4. Atmospheric Refraction and Scattering
points: **Atmospheric refraction** — bending of light through air layers of changing density causes **twinkling of stars** and the **Sun appearing before sunrise/after sunset** (advanced sunrise/delayed sunset).
**Tyndall effect** — scattering of light by fine particles/colloids.
**Scattering of light:** blue is scattered most (shorter wavelength) → **sky appears blue**; the **Sun looks reddish at sunrise/sunset** (blue scattered away, red reaches us).
The sky appears **dark/black** to an astronaut (no atmosphere to scatter).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Near point = 25 cm; image forms on retina by the eye lens.
Myopia → concave lens; Hypermetropia → convex lens; Presbyopia → bifocal.
Dispersion (VIBGYOR): red bends least, violet most.
Blue sky = scattering (blue scattered most); red sunset = blue scattered away.
Twinkling of stars & advanced sunrise = atmospheric refraction.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Myopia is corrected by a concave lens**; **hypermetropia by a convex lens** (do not swap).
**Violet bends the most, red the least** in a prism.
The sky is blue because **blue light is scattered the most** (shortest wavelength).
The **Sun appears red at sunrise/sunset** because blue is scattered away.
